 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGESH KHANNA  ORDER % 19.01.2023 1.

Petitioner files this petition for quashing of the FIR No.370/2018 under Section 376/323/506 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Paharganj against him and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The allegations in the aforesaid FIR are on the pretext of marriage, the petitioner made physical relations with respondent No.2.

It is the submission of the learned counsel for petitioner the FIR was a result of misunderstanding as all along the petitioner wish to marry respondent No.2 but due unavoidable circumstances, the marriage was delayed, but nevertheless during the pendency of FIR,
both of them had married on 25.03.2019 in Arya Samaj Mandir, Delhi and after their marriage, they are living peacefully for the last three years, hence this petition for quashing of the FIR.

3. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the FIR was registered due to some misunderstanding as she was apprehensive the petitioner would not marry her.
However, since both of them are now married and are living peacefully, she does not wish to pursue the FIR against her husband as it would detrimental to their married life.
She has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned ASC for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

5. Further in Mandar Deepak Pawar vs. The State of Maharashtra in CRL.A.442/2022; Anand D.V.
vs. State & Anr. in CRL.A.Nos.394-95/2021; Ganesh Shankar Pilane vs. The State of Maharashtra and Anr. in W.P.(CRL.)272/2022; Manteshwar Hanumantrao Kattimani vs. State of Maharashtra and Anr. 2016 SCC OnLine Bom 10581; and Capt. Simranjit Singh Sambhi vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
and Anr. CRL.M.C.2960/2021 the Courts have exercised power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the proceedings under Section 376 IPC on the facts mentioned therein.

Thus in view of submission so made; the law discussed above; the lodging of FIR by the prosecutrix being due to misunderstanding between them; both of them having married each other and are living peacefully, hence there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioner as it would never entail in conviction of petitioner herein and would be a sheer wastage of time.
7. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.370/2018 under Section 376/323/506 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Paharganj and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
